title: Outbound lists
blurb: Lists, profiles, penetration versus vertical, resets, and the guardrails around time and detection.
summary: Outbound dials a loaded list under a mode. Resets and ANI changes are explicit.

lessons.title: A list is not a campaign
objectives: Separate file, list, and running campaign
paragraphs: Outbound and autodial campaigns dial lists of contact records. The list has an order. The campaign has a run state and a dialing mode. Uploading a CSV does neither of those.

The disposition topic says you reset list position and dispositions on the lists currently loaded in that campaign. A list sitting in the library and a list loaded in the campaign are not the same moment.

lessons.title: Profiles filter the list the agent sees
objectives: Keep dialing mode on the campaign
paragraphs: Campaign profiles filter and sort lists, control agent pop-ups, and manage disposition counts. They also override defaults such as the ANI. One campaign, one profile. Workflow rules can swap the profile.
A filter on the profile changes which rows are eligible. It does not change list penetration versus vertical. That choice is the list dialing mode on the campaign.

lessons.title: List penetration and vertical dialing
objectives: Walk both list modes on paper
paragraphs: List penetration is the default. The dialer tries the first phone on every record, then the next phone on a later pass. Vertical dialing stays with one contact and moves across that contact's numbers before it moves on.

The community article's wording is easy to twist: it says the physical direction of list penetration is vertical, while the industry phrase vertical dialing means walking numbers across a record. Use the article's definitions, not the compass words. A final disposition stops every number on the record in either mode.
uncertain: The documentation portal has a vertical-dialing chapter. This lesson follows the community article's definitions because that page returned readable text. Confirm the portal chapter in your own admin guide.

left: Next pass waits until the record comes around

lessons.title: Reset is a loaded gun
paragraphs: Reset list position sends the dialer back to the top. Reset Disposition clears selected outcomes so those rows can dial again. Both act on lists currently loaded. The disposition topic says to reset only codes you know are safe.
A scheduled disposition update from CSV can also stamp codes, using a key field such as the phone column. The list details report is how you prove the stamp landed, for outbound.

lessons.title: Time zone and call analysis are guarded defaults
objectives: Refuse to invent the legal dialing hours
paragraphs: The campaign admin tree includes time zone dialing options, and the default-settings topic says call analysis and voice detection level ship with vendor defaults. Changing defaults can raise a compliance warning. The same topic says US domains watch abandon rate for 30 rolling days and UK domains for 24 hours, and that a Five9 representative sets which kind of domain you have.

This lab will not invent the legal calling window or the numeric abandon default. Both move, and both are jurisdiction-specific. Open the current page and the current rule before you widen either one.
uncertain: The exact hour-by-hour time zone matrix is in the campaign guide and was not copied here. Local telemarketing law is not Five9's default screen.

lessons.title: Call analysis is not a guarantee
objectives: Treat detection as a tuned field
Do not quote a fake accuracy
paragraphs: Call analysis and voice detection level are defaulted campaign fields. Product pages also list answering-machine detection and automatic voicemail as agent-efficiency tools. None of those pages give you a percent accuracy you can put in a contract.

A live person marked as a machine is a silent failure: the agent never hears them, or a voicemail template talks to a human. Treat detection as a tuned setting with a monitoring report, not as a fact about the callee.

lessons.title: Local caller ID is a profile choice
objectives: Keep STIR/SHAKEN as its own project
paragraphs: The outbound product page lists local caller ID as a business-efficiency tool, and campaign profiles are the documented place to override the default ANI. Showing a local number is a profile and number-plan problem, not a skill-group problem.
Certified Caller, on its own page, is the STIR/SHAKEN story. A local ANI does not by itself mean the call is signed. Keep those projects separate.
